samples.summary: Foldout-in-task exemption only covers <summary>; a click in the <details> BODY still ticks the task line
samples.evidence: The delta adds `summary` to the owned-control allowlist (preview.ts:276) precisely because a `<details>` block can nest inside a task `<li>` — the new test at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:196 asserts `summary.closest('li.task-list-item')` is non-null for `- [ ] todo\n\n  <details>…`. But the only structural guard after it is `const clickedItem = target.closest('li'); if (clickedItem && clickedItem !== item) return;` (preview.ts:297-298), which exempts nested list items only. The paragraph text inside the foldout body ("body" in that same fixture) is not an `li`, not an `a/button/summary`, and not a checkbox, so `target.closest('.task-list-item')` resolves it to the enclosing task item and the handler falls through to `this.onToggleTask?.(line, checked)` (preview.ts:317) → `setTaskChecked` (editor.ts:260), silently rewriting and syncing a task line the user never pointed at. The reasoning the diff gives for the summary exemption ("toggling would edit a line nobody pointed at") applies unchanged to the folded body, and the details plugin registers its rule with `alt: [… 'list']` (details-plugin.ts:105), so this nesting is a supported source shape. Same class of bypass for any non-`li` block nested in a task item (blockquote, table cell text).

samples.summary: Design doc still describes the pre-delta preview click contract
samples.evidence: docs/design/notes/notes.md:674-682 states "a delegated click anywhere on the item flips that line" and "The preview never updates its own DOM". After this delta neither is accurate: clicks inside `a`, `button` or `summary` are exempt (preview.ts:276), and the handler now cancels the click event to roll back the browser's own checkbox flip on every refusal path (preview.ts:286). The doc also records at line 669 that the list commands "rewrite only each line's marker prefix so the caret keeps its place in the text", which the new assoc-1 selection mapping in replacePrefixes (list-commands.ts:212-219) deliberately changes for a caret at column 0. This file is a NESTED design doc, so the backticked-path CI check does not recurse into it and nothing else will flag the drift.

samples.evidence: .note-preview.note-tasks-interactive li.task-list-item { cursor: pointer } applies to the whole task item and inherits into descendants, including a `<summary>`/foldout nested inside a task item, which after this delta no longer ticks (preview.ts:276). Verified in-repo, not taken on faith. preview.ts:276 adds the `a, button, summary` allowlist (with a comment justifying `summary` precisely because foldouts nest in task items), but the only structural guard afterwards is preview.ts:297-298 (`target.closest('li') !== item`), which exempts nested list items ONLY. Hand-tracing a single click on the `

` in an open `

` body nested in a task `li`: it is not a/button/summary (276 passes), onCheckbox is false, e.detail===1 (293 passes), closest('li') === item (298 passes), selection is collapsed (302 passes), and TASK_LINE_ATTR is set by the core rule at preview.ts:58-68, so control reaches this.onToggleTask(line, !checked) at preview.ts:317. That callback is a real document write: editor.ts:258-260 wires it to setTaskChecked(view, line + 1, checked) (list-commands.ts:294), so the task source line is rewritten and synced. The nesting is real and repo-attested: preview.test.ts:197-202 renders "- [ ] todo\n\n
… body …
" and asserts summary.closest('li.task-list-item') is non-null; details-plugin.ts:104-106 registers the rule with alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote','list'] and the plugin doc (lines 22-33) states the body is ordinary markdown, so details-inside-list-item is a supported shape. Same class applies to any non-li nested block (blockquote, table cell text). I weighed out-of-scope (incomplete exemption inside the changed handler smells like the correctness lens) but the bypass is only visible by combining the new allowlist with the pre-existing li-only guard and the out-of-diff consumer editor.ts:260 -> setTaskChecked; that is squarely "a guard with a reachable bypass" in this lane. No guard elsewhere covers non-li nested content, so already-guarded fails too. Nothing concretely refutes the finding.

finding.summary: Preview task-click handler swallows clicks on other interactive preview widgets nested in a task item (notably `<summary>` foldouts) and turns them into an unintended task toggle
finding.evidence: `onTaskClick` only exempts `target.closest('a, button')` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:283) and then calls `e.preventDefault()` before toggling (preview.ts:303). The preview also renders native disclosures via the pre-existing foldout feature: `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:110-115` emits `<details class="note-details">` / `<summary class="note-summary">`, and `detailsRule` trims the line before matching (details-plugin.ts:54), so a `<details>`/`<summary>` indented inside a task list item still parses. A click on such a `<summary>` resolves `closest('li')` to the same task `<li>`, passes every guard, gets `preventDefault()`d (so the disclosure never opens) and instead rewrites the source line — a document edit, synced to peers, from a click meant to expand a section. The same applies to any future non-a/button control the preview grows inside a list item. Fix belongs on the new exclusion list in preview.ts.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is false in this tree. `onTaskClick` exempts `summary` alongside `a` and `button`: `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:276` reads `if (target.closest('a, button, summary')) return;`, with the comment at preview.ts:272-275 naming exactly the foldout-inside-a-task-item case as its motivation. A repo-wide Grep for `closest('a, button` finds only that one source line (all other hits are `.agent-review/*` review artifacts), so no second copy of the handler carries the older `a, button` selector. The claimed `preventDefault()` before toggling is also mischaracterised: preview.ts:286 cancels only when the click landed on the checkbox (`if (onCheckbox) e.preventDefault();`), and the unconditional cancel at preview.ts:316 is downstream of the `summary` early return, so a summary click is neither cancelled nor turned into a source rewrite. The scenario is explicitly covered by a regression test at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:192-210, which confirms the nesting does occur (`summary.closest('li.task-list-item')` non-null) and then asserts `event.defaultPrevented === false` and no toggles. The details-plugin half of the evidence (details-plugin.ts:54 trimming, :110-115 emitting `note-details`/`note-summary`) is accurate, but it does not lead to the claimed defect. The remaining generalisation about "any future non-a/button control" concerns code that does not exist and is not a present defect. Cited line numbers 283/303 do not match the quoted code either.

finding.summary: New mutating API methods (list toggles, indent/outdent) and `setTaskChecked` dispatch without the read-only guard the sibling new code applies, and the notes editor never sets `EditorState.readOnly`
finding.evidence: `noteCheckboxInput` explicitly refuses to write when the doc is read-only or the view is non-editable (packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:25-30), but the five new `NoteEditorAPI` methods wired at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:581-585 call `toggleBulletList`/`indentList`/… which dispatch unconditionally (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:228-231, 289-299), as does `setTaskChecked` (list-commands.ts:290+). A grep for `EditorState.readOnly` across packages shows the editor only ever sets `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (editor.ts:413) — never the read-only facet — so `view.dispatch` from these commands mutates and syncs a read-only note. Today the only host that mounts read-only (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:352) renders no notes toolbar and never takes the API via `onEditorReady`, so I could not confirm a live caller; the exposure is that the API surface, which is public from `@wafflebase/notes`, now has more unguarded mutation entry points than before. Fix belongs on the new commands (or by adding `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` in editor.ts).

verdict.reason: Verified independently. (1) The notes editor never sets the EditorState.readOnly facet: a grep of `readOnly` across packages/notes yields only the initialize parameter and its derived uses (editor.ts:235,240,258,334), `EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly)` (editor.ts:413), the checkbox-input guard, and one test occurrence of the facet. (2) The five new API methods (editor.ts:581-585) funnel into replacePrefixes, which calls view.dispatch(... userEvent:'input') with no writability check (list-commands.ts:207-219, reached from toggleKind 230-252, shift 268-274, indentList/outdentList 277-286); setTaskChecked dispatches unconditionally as well (list-commands.ts:294-312). noteSync pushes any non-remote 'input' change into the store (note-sync.ts:68-111), so those paths would mutate and sync a read-only note. (3) The sibling new code does guard exactly this: checkbox-input.ts:24-30 checks both view.state.readOnly and the EditorView.editable facet, with a comment naming both non-writable modes, so the invariant is one the package asserts about itself. I searched for counterexamples in the commands themselves, the store layer (memory.ts:88, store.ts:84 have no writability flag), conditional API construction (editor.ts:573-585 are unconditional; only insertImageFiles is gated via uploadImage), and the frontend hosts, and found none. Reachability from a JS caller is unproven - the only read-only mount (shared-document.tsx:352) passes no onEditorReady and renders no notes toolbar, and the toolbar host (notes-detail.tsx:198-211) never sets readOnly - but the missing facet additionally leaves basicSetup's default keymap and the explicitly bound indentWithTab (editor.ts:372) unguarded, because @codemirror/commands commands check only state.readOnly, not EditorView.editable. So the fix location the reviewer names is right and covers more than the five methods. Nothing here refutes the absence claim.
